articles.title: Alteon raises $2.5 million to build aircraft aimed at months-long flight
articles.summary: India Business News: Alteon raises $2.5M pre-seed to develop autonomous aircraft using dynamic soaring wind energy for months-long flight; aims for energy-neutral ocean tests.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Bengaluru-based aerospace startup Alteon has raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Lachy Groom, an early Stripe executive and co-founder of robotics company Physical Intelligence. Together Fund, the operator-led venture firm co-founded by Girish Mathrubootham and Manav Garg, also participated.Alteon plans to use the capital to develop autonomous aircraft designed to remain airborne for months by extracting energy from winds over the ocean.Its immediate goal is to demonstrate “energy-neutral dynamic soaring.” This would require the aircraft to remain aloft without propulsion by gaining enough energy from changes in wind speed to sustain flight.Dynamic soaring is a technique used by albatrosses. It involves repeatedly moving between layers of air travelling at different speeds. This allows an aircraft to gain energy as it climbs, turns and dives. Alteon believes the technique could eventually overcome the fuel and battery limitations that restrict aircraft endurance.The startup said its aircraft completed multiple consecutive autonomous loops less than one metre above the open ocean during an offshore test in early August. The test showed that the aircraft could perform a demanding low-altitude manoeuvre in real offshore conditions, it said.It did not, however, demonstrate sustained flight using wind energy alone. That is the next technical hurdle Alteon is working to clear.“Building aircraft that fly for over a year using it is not a matter of a single technical breakthrough but a matter of solving a range of challenging engineering problems across autonomy, structures, aero and more,” founder Samay Sanghvi said. “As we go from measuring flight time in hours to months, the standard everything has to meet goes up with it.”Sanghvi began working on the project in 2023, shortly after leaving high school, and formally founded Alteon in 2025. The company said it now has a 20-member team in Bengaluru. It had previously received backing from Emergent Ventures and investor 1517.Alteon sees potential applications in weather and ocean mapping, tracking ships and fishing activity, monitoring critical infrastructure, defence and search-and-rescue operations. It has not announced customers or a timeline for commercial deployment.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Nearly 10% of FMCG distributor applications fail FSSAI checks: Report
articles.summary: India Business News: AuthBridge report: 9.8% of FMCG distributor onboarding applications in FY26 failed FSSAI checks; 8% had ID mismatches and 4.5% GST issues.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nearly one in 10 FMCG distributor onboarding applications checked by verification firm AuthBridge in FY26 failed food safety licence checks, with expired licences, missing product approvals and invalid certificates among the problems detected.The findings are based on about 3,500 applications processed through AuthBridge’s platform for FMCG companies across India during FY 2025-26. The dataset covered tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 distribution networks and was drawn from actual company-led onboarding checks rather than a survey, AuthBridge said. It did not identify the FMCG companies involved.Around 9.8% of the applications failed checks against Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) records. Another 8% showed identity mismatches across regulatory documents, while 4.5% failed goods and services tax (GST) compliance checks.These categories are not mutually exclusive. A single application could carry multiple flags, such as an expired FSSAI licence and a GST registration issued for a different state. The percentages, therefore, cannot be added to determine an overall failure rate.The FSSAI-related failures included expired licences, licences that did not cover the relevant product category, and invalid or forged certificates. GST issues included cancelled registrations, incorrect certificates and registrations submitted for the wrong state.Cross-document checks also found cases where addresses differed across GST and FSSAI records, or where the legal name on a PAN did not match GST records. The report said such discrepancies could result from data-entry or documentation errors, but could also point to dormant entities or identity fraud.Another pattern identified was what the report called “trade identity fraud”. In such cases, a business sought a distributor code under one trade name while submitting a GST identification number belonging to another legal entity. Such discrepancies may escape manual scrutiny unless information declared by the applicant is matched against official records.“Trust cannot be established through documents alone,” AuthBridge founder and CEO Ajay Trehan said. He called for companies to monitor regulatory records, identities and financial health throughout their relationship with distributors, rather than limiting checks to onboarding.Weak screening could expose FMCG companies to credit losses, tax disputes, regulatory scrutiny, product recalls and supply-chain disruption, the report said. It recommended live regulatory checks, cross-document identity matching and periodic monitoring of compliance and credit records.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US construction spending drops to nearly three-year low in July
articles.summary: construction spending unexpectedly fell in July, hitting the lowest level in nearly three years as higher mortgage ‌rates weighed on single-family homebuildi...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Sept 1 (Reuters) - U.S. construction spending unexpectedly fell in July, hitting the lowest level in nearly three years as higher mortgage ‌rates weighed on single-family homebuilding.

The Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Tuesday ‌that construction spending dropped 0.5% to $2.158 trillion, the lowest level since October 2023. Data for June ​was revised higher to show construction spending unchanged instead of dipping 0.1%, as previously reported. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast construction spending would be unchanged in July.

Construction spending plunged 3.8% on a year-over-year basis in July. Spending on private ‌construction projects decreased 0.5% after ⁠easing 0.1% in June. Investment in residential construction tumbled 1.3%. Spending on single-family housing projects dropped 3.2%. On a year-over-year ⁠basis, it plummeted 6.5% in July.

Homebuilding is also being squeezed by a glut of unsold single-family houses. The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed-rate mortgage is hovering ​near ​a one-year high of 6.66%, data from ​mortgage finance agency Freddie Mac showed. ‌It has surged by almost 70 basis points since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran started in late February.

Spending on multi-family housing units, which account for a small share of the housing market, rose 0.2% in July.

Investment in private nonresidential structures such as power plants and factories increased 0.4% in July. Spending on ‌power plants rose 0.5%. But outlays on ​factory projects dropped 0.8% in July and 21.7% ​on a year-over-year basis as ​the boost from the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act fades. ‌That fading momentum has more than offset ​some of the ​lift from an artificial intelligence buildout. Investment in nonresidential structures contracted in the second quarter, logging its 10th straight quarterly decline.

Investment in public construction ​projects fell 0.2% in ‌July after gaining 0.1% in June. State and local government construction ​spending was unchanged, while outlays on federal government projects declined 3.5%.

(Reporting ​by Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Paul Simao)

articles.title: How soaring Treasury yields could hit your finances
articles.summary: Bond yields rise as bond prices fall, impacting everything from stock and bond markets to loan rates and savings returns.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

When Treasury yields reach multiyear highs, some investors get nervous. Higher bond yields are triggered by lower bond prices, and the effects are felt across the financial spectrum: from investing in stocks and bonds to borrowing costs and savings returns.

Global bond yields are gripping markets, jumping back to their highest level in almost two decades as higher oil prices, inflation fears, and heavy government borrowing continue to add pressure.

Here is how rising Treasury yields could impact your finances, including mortgages, credit cards, and car loans.

The Treasury yield is the return an investor receives for lending money to the government — for example, 4.5% on a 10-year Treasury note.

If you invest $1,000 in a 10-year Treasury with a rate of 4.5%, you will receive $45 in interest annually over the next 10 years — and receive your initial $1,000 investment back when the bond matures in 10 years.

If bond yields rise, prices fall. If bond yields fall, prices rise.

If rates go up, say to 5.5%, your Treasury note becomes less valuable because investors can earn a higher rate on newly issued Treasurys. If you sell your bond, rather than hold it to maturity, you will lose money.

If rates go down , for example, to 3.5%, your Treasury note becomes more valuable. If you sell the note before maturity, you'll get more than the $1,000 you invested.

Of course, in either case, if you sell, you won't get your $45 in annual interest any longer.

Changes in interest rates and prices only impact your investment if you sell before the bond matures.

The bond market is reacting to the lingering conflict in the Middle East. With hope for a resolution fading, the war is keeping inflation fears active as gas prices continue to rise. The Consumer Price Index rose 3.8% in April — the largest gain in three years — while gas prices surged over 28%. Prices continued to soar in May and then cooled in June as energy prices fell. However, renewed tensions with Iran are bringing uncertainty back to the market.

Inflation reduces consumer buying power, and Treasurys are reflecting that concern.

A growing government deficit is also dulling bond market enthusiasm.

The Wall Street futures market is also beginning to suspect that the Federal Reserve's next move may be a rate hike, rather than an interest rate reduction.

How higher Treasury yields impact bond investors

As noted above, rising Treasury yields cut the market value of existing bonds. New investments may move to just-issued bonds rather than to holdings offered for sale in the secondary market.

How higher Treasury yields impact stock investors

Higher bond yields put pressure on equity returns. For one thing, companies have to pay more to borrow money.

Also, if an investor can get a risk-free return of 5% or more from the government, equities may seem less appealing. Stock market volatility can also dampen enthusiasm for riskier investments such as tech stocks.

How higher Treasury yields impact borrowing costs

The cost of borrowing money increases for the government and households as well. Rising Treasury yields:

Expand the federal deficit as the cost of paying down debt increases. With the total national debt at $40 trillion , a 1% increase in interest rates would add roughly $4 trillion in interest costs over the next 10 years.

Are likely to cause mortgage rates, priced to 10-year Treasury notes, to continue rising.

Can make other consumer borrowing more expensive, contributing to higher auto loan rates and credit card APRs.

How higher Treasury yields impact savings returns

One positive result of higher Treasury yields can be the upward momentum to savings returns. While short-term savings accounts are driven more by the prime rate and Fed rate moves, longer-term savings may be influenced by multiyear bonds.

How your 401(k) may be affected by Treasury yields

Mutual funds, target-date funds, and exchange-traded funds that invest in stocks may experience volatility. Bond funds, which are allocated to bundles of bonds, may also see some short-term losses.

How Treasury yields compare to Fed rates

The Federal Reserve works with short-term interest rates. Treasury yields span multiple time horizons. Fed rate moves ultimately steer the prime rate, which can impact consumer debt such as variable-rate credit cards (though little impact has been seen lately). Treasury yields mostly drive longer-term debt, such as mortgage rates.

Depending on your situation, here are actions to consider as Treasury yields rise:

As a stock investor : Consider your current balance of investments, particularly growth stocks with already high valuations. Consider dividend-paying value stocks with strong cash flow and low debt. Expect volatility and resist making rash moves.

As a bond investor : Review your bond holdings and consider overall duration. Short-term bond holdings will be more resilient. Long-maturity Treasury funds may see sharp losses. However, new bonds you buy will pay more interest. Consider a bond ladder with varying Treasury maturities. Consider TIPS, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities.

As a 401(k) or IRA investor : Having a proper mix of stocks, bonds, and cash in your retirement account can help you weather interest rate changes and market volatility. Remember, with a 401(k), you are contributing to your retirement savings with every paycheck. Ask your provider for an account review and suggestions for improvements that match the risk you are willing to take. For your IRA, ask your investment advisor if you are properly positioned.

As a saver : Look for opportunities to enhance your return. If you see a favorable rate, you may want to move cash into higher-yielding accounts, such as CDs and short-term Treasurys.

As a borrower : Consider paying down variable-rate accounts, such as credit cards and HELOCs. Mortgage rates may move higher, but bond yields are unpredictable. Be financially prepared to make a move when you find a mortgage rate that fits your budget.

Understanding the Fed's rate decisions: Do we want high or low interest rates​?

The Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions can directly impact your wallet. So what's better: high or low interest rates?

U.S. debt tops $40 trillion. How soaring federal debt affects you personally.

The U.S. national debt has hit $40 trillion. What does that mean for the stock and bond markets — and the cost of living?

How the Fed's rate decision affects your bank accounts, loans, credit cards, and investments

Here's how the Fed's rate decision could impact savings products, various types of loans, and credit cards.

How rising national debt can affect your finances

The national debt may be hard to conceptualize, but economists say its explosive growth has the potential to have major impacts on the economy and your wallet.

How does inflation impact savings and CD rates?

Understanding the relationship between savings/CD rates and inflation can help you maximize your interest earnings. Here’s how inflation impacts savings account and CD rates.

High-yield savings account vs. Treasury bill: Which is right for you?

If you're looking to earn a high interest rate on your savings, two options to consider are high-yield savings accounts and Treasury bills. Learn more about the differences between T-bills vs. savings accounts and which one is best for you.

articles.title: UPI gets festive boost: Digital payments hit a record 24.51 billion transactions in August
articles.summary: India Business News: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) hit a new monthly high in August, with transaction volumes crossing 24 billion for the first time in a month and reac.
articles.body: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) hit a new monthly high in August, with transaction volumes crossing 24 billion for the first time in a month and reaching 24.51 billion, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on Tuesday.The record came as transaction activity picked up during the festive period, particularly around Raksha Bandhan. UPI processed transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore during the month, taking the value close to the record Rs 29.9 lakh crore recorded in May and July 2026.The August volume was 22% higher than the 19.63 billion transactions recorded in the same month last year. It also marked a rise from 23.66 billion transactions in July, 22.72 billion in June and 23.2 billion in May.In value terms, August transactions were up 20% from Rs 24.85 lakh crore a year earlier.Festive activity adds to UPI momentumThe rise in transaction volumes in August was further supported by Raksha Bandhan, which led to higher peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers and small-ticket gifting, Cashfree Payments co-founder Reeju Datta said."The volume growth in August was further bolstered by festive activity such as Raksha Bandhan, which naturally drove a surge in everyday peer-to-peer (P2P) transfers and small-ticket gifting, and consistent aggregate transaction value with an increase in volume over the past three months underscores the expanding reach and depth of the UPI ecosystem," Cashfree Payments co-founder Reeju Datta said.Datta said the upcoming festive season presented an exciting growth frontier.Network People Services Technologies (NPST) co-founder and CEO Deepak Chand Thakur said the next phase of growth would come as newer UPI use cases develop."As the festive season approaches and new use cases such as credit on UPI start to mature, continued investment in resilient, intelligent infrastructure will be key to sustaining India's leadership in digital payments, Network People Services Technologies (NPST) co-founder and CEO Deepak Chand Thakur said.From 1.78 crore transactions to 24,162 croreThe latest monthly record comes as UPI continues to expand rapidly since its launch on August 25, 2016.Its annual transaction volume has grown from 1.78 crore in 2016-17 to more than 24,162 crore in 2025-26, an almost 13,000-fold increase.Transaction value has also climbed sharply over the decade, from Rs 0.07 lakh crore in FY17 to around Rs 314 lakh crore in FY26 — an increase of more than 4,000 times.The growth trajectory reached another milestone in May 2026, when monthly UPI transactions crossed 2,300 crore for the first time. The month recorded 2,320 crore transactions.UPI now accepted in 11 countriesUPI's expansion has also extended beyond India. The payment system is now accepted in 11 countries, with Uzbekistan the latest addition.The other countries where UPI is accepted are Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, and Greece.NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is the umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India. It runs UPI, which enables real-time payments between peers and at merchants' end while making purchases.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Whatfix cofounder, CEO Khadim Batti dies at 51
articles.summary: India Business News: Whatfix cofounder and CEO Khadim Batti dies at 49 after cardiac arrest; he led the digital adoption SaaS firm’s global growth and $125M Series E funding.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Khadim Batti, cofounder and chief executive of enterprise software company Whatfix, died on Tuesday following a cardiac arrest. He was 51.Batti co-founded Whatfix with his longtime colleague Vara Kumar Namburu in Bengaluru in 2014. He led its growth into one of India’s prominent enterprise software-as-a-service companies, serving large businesses worldwide.Whatfix makes digital adoption software. Its technology sits on top of workplace applications and provides employees with on-screen guidance, training and analytics as they complete tasks. Batti had described the core product as “a GPS for software.”Batti and Kumar first worked together at Huawei, where they spent nearly a decade building large-scale technology products. They left the company around 2010 to start an enterprise focused on search engine optimisation for small businesses. A feature designed to guide users through that product eventually became the foundation for Whatfix.Under Batti’s leadership, Whatfix expanded across India, the US, Europe, Singapore and Australia. Its $125-million in 2024, led by Warburg Pincus with participation from SoftBank Vision Fund 2, valued the company at around $900 million. By November 2025, Whatfix had more than 900 employees.Batti was also closely involved with India’s SaaS and AI founder communities. He served on the governing council of SaaSBoomi and was among the founding members of AIBoomi, a community focused on AI-first products built from India. He was also an angel investor and mentor to several founders.Avinash Raghava, CEO and founding volunteer at SaaSBoomi, said Batti’s journey with Whatfix had inspired many entrepreneurs. “A wonderful friend. A generous mentor. Someone who always made time for the ecosystem and showed up for founders with warmth and sincerity,” Raghava said in a post. “We have lost someone very special today.”Below is the official statement from Whatfix, in full:It is with deep sorrow that we confirm the unexpected passing of our beloved co-founder and CEO, Khadim Batti, who suffered a sudden cardiac arrest today. The company requests the media and the public to respect the privacy of Khadim’s family during this difficult time.A visionary leader known for his transformative impact on the global enterprise SaaS landscape, Khadim’s passion, clarity, and conviction shaped not just Whatfix, but everyone who had the privilege of meeting him. He inspired entrepreneurs beyond technology to dream big and pursue their ambitions with conviction. His legacy lies in the resilient organization and deeply committed leadership team he built. Our leadership team remains steadfast in carrying his vision forward.We remain united in the vision and values Khadim championed.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Qualcomm leads Rs 583 cr Ultrahuman funding round
articles.summary: India Business News: Qualcomm leads Ultrahuman’s Rs 583 crore funding round, backing founder Mohit Kumar as the wearable health tech firm scales products and growth.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Wearable health startup Ultrahuman is stitching together a Rs 583 crore led by Qualcomm Ventures, regulatory filings sourced via Tofler showed.The fundraise comes as the company swung to a Rs 176 crore loss in FY26 from a Rs 73 crore profit a year earlier, according to provisional financials attached to the filings.Qualcomm Ventures, the chipmaker’s investment arm, is expected to invest about Rs 143 crore. Investment firm Alpha Wave will put in Rs 114 crore, while US laboratory-services company Labcorp will invest around Rs 95 crore. Existing investor Blume Ventures is contributing about Rs 90 crore.Zomato founder Deepinder Goyal is participating with Rs 47.4 crore. Nexus Venture Partners and Krypton Fund will invest Rs 18.9 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively. Steadview Capital, GGM Family Trust, InCred Wealth and other investors are also participating.The funding was first reported by Entrackr.The valuation report also provides a first look at Ultrahuman’s provisional FY26 performance. Its revenue rose 15% to Rs 651 crore, while total income increased to about Rs 688 crore from Rs 581 crore. But Ebitda swung to a Rs 133 crore loss from a Rs 35 crore profit. The company posted a net loss of Rs 176 crore, compared with a Rs 73 crore profit in FY25. The figures include a Rs 62 crore exceptional item.For the June quarter, Ultrahuman reported revenue of Rs 51.8 crore and a net loss of Rs 103.6 crore, the management-provided figures showed.The funding also comes as Ultrahuman rebuilds its presence in the US. The valuation report said its Ring Air is no longer sold there following a 2025 patent ruling, while the redesigned Ring Pro was launched in the market in April.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Yuma Energy raises $35 million from Magna for battery-swap expansion
articles.summary: India Business News: Yuma Energy raises $35m Series A from Magna to expand its battery-swapping network across India, aiming for EBITDA-positive FY27 after 60m swaps.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Battery-swapping provider Yuma Energy has raised $35 million from existing backer Magna International to expand its network across India.The company plans to enter new markets, add infrastructure and serve a wider mix of individual EV users, fleet operators and vehicle manufacturers. It is also targeting Ebitda-positive operations in FY27. Yuma did not disclose its valuation or other terms of the transaction.Yuma said it has completed more than 60 million battery swaps. Its network comprises over 100,000 batteries and 2,500 charging units spread across more than 400 touch points in 18 cities.“Crossing 60 million swaps was a defining moment for us,” said Muthu Subramanian, managing director and general manager of Yuma Energy. He added that the company would use Magna’s support to accelerate its infrastructure rollout and deepen partnerships with fleets and original equipment manufacturers.Battery swapping allows an EV user to exchange a depleted battery for a charged one instead of waiting for it to recharge. The model is particularly relevant for electric two- and three-wheelers used by delivery workers and commercial fleets, where charging downtime can affect daily earnings and vehicle utilisation.Yuma was launched in February 2023 as a joint venture between global automotive supplier Magna and shared electric-mobility company Yulu. Its network initially supported Yulu’s fleet but was also designed to serve other EV makers and mobility operators.Magna’s regulatory filings previously showed that it held a 51% controlling interest in the battery-swapping entity after contributing $52 million, while Yulu held the remaining 49% in exchange for assets and intellectual property. Yuma did not say whether the latest investment would alter that ownership structure.The company has also been adding capabilities beyond operating swapping stations. In February 2025, it acquired Chennai-based battery technology startup Grinntech to strengthen its battery design, research and manufacturing operations.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Zetwerk design-led contracts jump to 14% of manufacturing GMV
articles.summary: India Business News: Zetwerk’s ODM (design-led) contracts rose to 13.93% of manufacturing GMV in FY26 as it boosts in-house design; IPO includes Rs 2,600 crore fresh issue.
articles.body: BENGALURU: IPO-bound Zetwerk is taking on more product-design work instead of only manufacturing to customer specifications. Original design manufacturing (ODM) contracts accounted for 13.9% of its manufacturing-business gross merchandise value (GMV) in FY26, up from 8.3% a year earlier.The share had risen gradually from 7.6% in FY23 to 8.1% in FY24 and 8.3% in FY25, before the sharper increase last year, the company’s updated draft IPO papers showed.Under an ODM contract, Zetwerk is responsible for designing a product in addition to manufacturing it. This differs from build-to-print work, where it produces components according to drawings and specifications supplied by a customer.GMV refers to the total value of goods and services transacted on Zetwerk’s platform, including taxes. It is not the same as revenue booked by the company.Zetwerk said it has developed in-house engineering and design capabilities for components used in transformers for AI data centres, process plant machinery, metal manufacturing and defence applications. It has also invested selectively in assembly and finishing facilities as larger customers sought more integrated manufacturing support.The company plans to expand ODM by hiring engineers, strengthening its design capabilities and building specialised production assets. It will focus on categories where design complexity can provide an advantage. Zetwerk said it will continue using its third-party supplier network for ODM projects instead of making all such products at its own facilities.It also plans to expand category-specific design libraries and standard product platforms that can be customised for different customers.The filing, citing a Redseer report commissioned by the company, said customers may pay a premium for design and product co-creation. Switching an ODM supplier can also require re-engineering, potentially making these customer relationships stickier.However, Zetwerk did not separately disclose the revenue or profitability of its ODM contracts. The contribution margin of its wider manufacturing business eased to 12.40% in FY26 from 13.43% in FY25, even as the ODM share increased.Manufacturing-business segment revenue rose to Rs 9,374.7 crore in FY26 from Rs 6,249. crore a year earlier. It accounted for 58.9% of Zetwerk’s revenue from continuing operations. Zetwerk’s proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to Rs 2,600 crore and an offer for sale of up to 9.68 crore shares by existing shareholders.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Airline credit cards provide rewards and benefits tied to specific airlines. For example, Delta credit cards earn Delta SkyMiles on eligible purchases and offer certain benefits if you fly Delta. That could include a free checked bag or boarding the plane quicker.

These cards are meant for travelers loyal to one airline, or who at least fly a specific airline most of the time.

There are two primary types of airline credit cards:

A credit card company issues a co-branded airline card in partnership with an airline. For example, Chase issues the Southwest Rapid Rewards Plus Credit Card in partnership with Southwest Airlines.

Co-branded cards make sense if you're loyal to a specific airline because they typically have rewards and benefits tied to that airline. That could include receiving a free checked bag, priority boarding, or something similar. Your primary redemption option is using rewards for award flights on your connected airline.

General travel cards earn rewards that can be redeemed through travel portals or transferred to multiple airline loyalty programs. This gives you more flexibility over using your rewards since you aren't tied to one airline. However, you'll miss out on perks like free checked bags and priority boarding.

What to look for in an airline credit card

Consider these features as you compare airline credit cards:

Welcome bonus: A welcome offer or sign-up bonus can provide loads of value for signing up for a card and completing specific requirements. It's often best to time new card applications with upcoming large purchases to help complete welcome bonus spending requirements as a new card member.

Rewards: It makes sense to find a card with a rewards rate that aligns with your spending habits. If you drive a lot for work, earning more rewards on gas could make sense. The same could be said for dining out, buying groceries, paying for streaming services, and other similar spending categories.

Benefits: Getting a free checked bag is one of the best benefits of airline cards, but you might also be interested in airline lounge access, priority boarding, elite status, and other perks.

Fees: If you plan to travel internationally, it helps to have a card with no foreign transaction fees.

Redemption options: The primary redemption option for airline cards is using rewards for award flights. General travel credit cards can provide more flexibility with redemption options.

Whether or not you should get an airline credit card comes down to the value you expect to receive.

Frequent travelers who spend money on airfare regularly can absolutely benefit from earning rewards on those tickets. However, the right credit card with airfare rewards can also help you save money even if you only travel a few times yearly.

Here are a few questions to ask yourself before opening a new airline card:

How often do you travel? Frequent fliers may want to prioritize cards that earn bonus miles on airfare, while occasional travelers may prefer to earn bonus points or miles at grocery stores, gas stations, and restaurants to put toward future flights.

What's your budget? If a steep annual fee or welcome bonus offer will push you to spend more than you can afford, it's better to forgo big rewards and avoid taking on debt. Even the best travel rewards can't beat the high cost of credit card interest charges.

How's your credit? Credit cards with airline rewards typically require good credit to qualify. If you don't already have a solid score, consider a credit-building card instead to build up a positive payment history and establish good credit habits. Later, you can put those habits to good use while earning travel rewards.

What travel benefits do you want? Plenty of travel rewards cards come with credits, complimentary lounge access, status, bonuses, and other perks that can help you save money when moving through the airport or on the go. But think about the travel expenses you already have to find your savings sweet spot. Maybe you're already a TSA PreCheck user, for example, and check bags every time you fly. A card that can offset your regular purchases is a great way to save money — as long as that value is more than the annual fee cost.

Is it worth it to get an airline credit card? Here's what to keep in mind.

Flight perks: Many credit cards for frequent flyer miles offer great benefits, including free checked baggage, priority boarding, inflight discounts, and other freebies that can save you money and elevate your flight experience.

Large welcome bonuses: Many of the best credit cards for earning airline miles offer sizable welcome bonuses, some of which are sufficient to cover more than one roundtrip domestic flight.

Potential for elite status: Some of the best miles credit cards offer a fast track to elite status with your everyday spending. Loyalty to a particular airline could open the doors to even more perks, such as complimentary upgrades and better boarding positions.

Limited flexibility: Unlike general travel credit cards, a credit card with flight rewards typically limits how you can use your miles. While some may let you book hotels, rental cars, and vacation packages, you may lose value compared to using your rewards for award flights. Remember, too, that award flights aren't completely free — you'll still need to pay taxes and fees.

Award availability: Earning enough miles to cover an award flight doesn't guarantee you'll be able to book one. Some airlines limit the number of seats available for award flights, so you may still need to pay cash unless you have some flexibility with your travel dates and times.

Potential for devaluation: Airlines occasionally introduce new policies that can devalue their rewards currency. In other words, you may work hard to amass a trove of miles, only to learn that they're less valuable than you thought.

Many travel rewards programs — like Chase Ultimate Rewards, Capital One Travel, and American Express Membership Rewards — allow you to transfer your points to airline partners, often at a 1:1 ratio. Here's a rundown of each program's current airline partners:

Say, for example, you're a Southwest Rapid Rewards member and often travel to and from locations serviced by the airline.

You may get the best value from a Southwest credit card, with rewards and benefits designed to help you earn status, priority, and more with the airline. But you should also consider a Chase travel card, as Southwest Rapid Rewards is a transfer partner and the issuer offers a wide range of rewards categories and benefits that extend beyond the specific airline.

What is the best credit card to buy airline tickets?

If you aren't loyal to a specific airline, it's best to use a general travel credit card to book your flights. Cards like the Chase Sapphire Preferred and American Express Gold Card provide elevated rewards on flights purchased directly from airlines, making it easy to earn valuable points regardless of the airline you fly.

It varies by airline, but many airline rewards currencies are worth at least one cent per mile. That means 10,000 miles could equal $100, depending on the loyalty program and the specific redemption method.

You can calculate how much your miles are worth for airfare by dividing the cash value of a flight by the total number of miles it would take to book the same flight. For example, $500 divided by 50,000 miles equals $0.01, or one cent per mile.

Is a travel credit card worth the annual fee?

It's worth the annual fee if you get enough value from its rewards and benefits to offset the cost each year. For example, the Capital One Venture X offers 10,000 anniversary miles and an annual $300 travel credit for Capital One Travel bookings. Without considering any other rewards or perks, you already have enough value from these two benefits to offset the $395 annual fee.

What is the best travel credit card for students?

One of the best travel credit cards for students is the Bank Of America® Travel Rewards For Students. This card provides valuable points for making eligible purchases, including travel purchases, and you can redeem your points to pay for flights, hotel stays, cruises, and more. Even better, there are no annual or foreign transaction fees.

We researched co-branded airline credit cards from major card issuers to find the best airline credit cards. We did not research every available credit card or include business credit cards in our research.

We added airline cards to a rubric to compare their perks, benefits, fees, welcome offers, and other features. Our analysis also considered the best travel credit cards, many of which can transfer rewards to airline loyalty programs.

Our final list of the best airline credit cards is based on our rubrics, research, and expert opinion.

And best of all, you'll get a $99 Companion Fare each account anniversary when you spend at least $6,000 over the account year before.

What to look for in a Bank of America card

The best way to find the right Bank of America card is by comparing your spending and your budget to the card's rewards, benefits, and cost.

If you travel often, for example, you may want a card with top rewards on your travel spending or benefits like lounge access and annual statement credits to help you save on each trip. If you're looking for savings on regular purchases like groceries and gas, you might prefer a card with flat rewards or specific bonus categories that target your most frequent budget items.

Also consider the annual fee. Many Bank of America cards have no annual fee, which can be great for maximizing your spending without giving up any rewards value to the fee cost. But if you are willing to pay an annual fee, you may score some valuable added perks in exchange, especially for travel.

Finally, think about whether you'll benefit from an introductory 0% APR. A significant portion of Bank of America cards have a 0% APR offer for new cardholders. If you know you'll benefit from no interest for the first several months or you have existing debt you want to pay off with a balance transfer, this is a factor to consider.

One of the most underrated benefits of opening a Bank of America card is the boosted rewards you can get with BofA Rewards.

If you have an eligible Bank of America checking account and you have a qualifying balance across both your Bank of America deposit accounts and Merrill investment accounts, you can qualify for BofA Rewards. There are multiple tiers based on your combined balances. These tiers determine the boost you can earn on your credit card rewards:

Member tier: 10% rewards bonus; no minimum balance

Preferred Plus tier: 25% rewards bonus; requires at least $30,000 in combined balances

Preferred Honors tier: 50% rewards bonus; requires at least $100,000 in combined balances

Premier tier: 75% rewards bonus; requires at least a $1 million in combined balances

Say, for example, you qualify for the Premier tier 75% boost and you have a Bank of America Unlimited Cash Rewards Credit Card. Typically, that card earns 1.5% cash back on every purchase. With your 75% boost, you'll instead earn 2.62% cash back on everything you buy. If you normally spend $15,000 on your card in a year, you could increase your annual rewards from $225 to $393 — just with your existing bank and investment account balances.

Bank of America offers several types of credit cards that are best suited for different types of spenders. Here's a look at some of the most common types of Bank of America credit cards:

Bank of America offers two types of cash-back cards, which can both offer great savings on your spending. One has tiered bonus categories with boosted rewards on specific purchases, like dining out at restaurants or fueling up at the gas station. This can be a good option if your most frequent purchases fall into bonus categories and you don't mind spending a bit of time figuring out how to best maximize your rewards.

The other offers a flat cash-back percentage on every purchase. This might be a better option if you don't want to worry about bonus categories, or if you're looking for a card to supplement other rewards cards that do have bonus categories.

Bank of America's travel credit cards offer uncomplicated rewards and redemptions. These Bank of America cards range in price from $0 to $550. Their rewards are pretty similar with a flat 1.5x points on every purchase, though some have slightly higher rewards for travel and dining purchases or Bank of America Travel Center spending.

The biggest difference — and the best way to get value from these cards — is the benefits. You won't get many added benefits from Bank of America's no-fee travel cards, but the higher-fee options offer statement credits for airline incidentals, lounge access, better redemption rates for points, and big welcome bonus offers.

Bank of America® Travel Rewards for Students

Several different types of Bank of America cards also have great 0% APR intro offers for new cardholders. In general, the 0% APR you'll get with a Bank of America card applies to both new purchases and balance transfers, though you must make the balance transfer within 60 days of account opening. The Bank of America credit card with the longest 0% APR period today is the BankAmericard, though this card doesn't offer any ongoing rewards or benefits after the intro period.

With any 0% APR card, it's important to pay down your balance by the end of the introductory period. After that, any amount you have left will accrue interest at your card's ongoing interest rate, which may reach well over 20% APR.

Bank of America partners with a few airlines to issue co-branded airline credit cards, including Alaska Airlines (along with Hawaiian Airlines), Spirit Airlines, Allegiant Air, and Flying Blue from KLM and Air France.

These cards earn rewards under each airline's loyalty program, which you can redeem for flights or other travel with the airline. That's different from standard Bank of America travel card rewards, which you can redeem with the issuer directly. A co-branded airline card can be a good idea if you're a frequent traveler and you prefer flying with a specific airline. These cards typically come with added benefits when you travel, like in-flight discounts, priority boarding, free checked bags, lounge access or discounted access, and more.

Free Spirit® Travel More World Elite Mastercard®

Adding a Bank of America card to your wallet can be a great way to earn rewards on your spending, secure a great 0% APR offer, or get some valuable travel benefits.

But you should always compare the potential value you may get from a new rewards card to your regular spending. If you already earn similar rewards with a different card or the Bank of America card you're considering doesn't maximize how you already spend money, it may not be the best option long term.

One of the best reasons to open a Bank of America card is if you already use the bank for your savings or investments. Qualifying BofA Rewards customers can multiply cash-back or points rewards with eligible cards by up to 75%. A Bank of America card that regularly earns 1.5% cash back on every purchase, for example, would earn 2.62% on every purchase at the highest tier. That's a better rewards rate than you'll find from nearly any other flat cash-back card today.

A Bank of America card may not be a good option for you if you don't already have a good credit score. Many top cards from the issuer require great credit, so you'll need to build your credit history before you apply for the best chances of approval. However, you can use a Bank of America secured credit card as an option to help build credit while you earn rewards.

The best Bank of America card for you depends on your goals and spending habits. Our overall pick is the Bank of America Customized Cash Rewards card, because it offers a mix of great rewards, common cash-back categories, 0% APR, and no annual fee. But before you apply, make sure you compare different options with varying rewards and benefits to determine which one offers the most value.

What is the easiest credit card to get with Bank of America?

In general, Bank of America credit cards require good-to-excellent credit for the best chances of approval. If you don't already have a solid credit score, consider secured versions of popular Bank of America cards, which are specifically designed to help you build credit. Here are some secured options from the issuer; each of these cards requires a refundable security deposit of at least $200 after approval:

Bank of America® Unlimited Cash Rewards Secured

Bank of America® Customized Cash Rewards Secured

Does applying for a Bank of America credit card hurt your credit?

Anytime you apply for a new credit card, you'll undergo a hard credit check, which can have a temporary negative impact on your credit score. However, you can build your credit back up and increase it as you use your new card responsibly and make your payments on time.

Our picks for the best Bank of America credit cards are all among the top-rated options using our comprehensive credit card rubric. To determine these credit card ratings, we look at a variety of factors. While those factors vary depending on the specific category, we look at details like annual fee, APR, introductory 0% APR offers, rewards, redemption options, and more.

Because we rate cards by category, you'll also find many of the cards on this list among our top picks in their respective credit card categories — such as best travel credit cards, best cash-back credit cards, and others.

For our complete list above, we factor in superlatives that we believe cover a broad range of Bank of America cards and what cardholders are seeking when considering a Bank of America credit card. From there, we use a combination of our objective rating system and our expert judgement to choose a final list of the best Bank of America cards.

Business credit cards function similarly to personal credit cards. They allow you to make eligible purchases on credit, which you then need to pay back within a certain amount of time. There are different types or categories of business credit cards, including travel cards, cash-back cards, secured cards, and corporate cards.

Travel credit cards: These cards make sense if you want to earn travel rewards points or miles on your business spending. Rewards can be used for travel-related redemptions, including flights, hotel stays, and car rentals. This may be a good option for you if you travel often for work.

Cash-back credit cards: You can typically redeem cash-back rewards for statement credits and gift cards. In some cases, you could also receive deposits into an eligible checking or savings account. Cash-back cards are a good choice if you have variable business expenses, especially if they fall in common categories like dining at restaurants, gas, software, or office supplies.

Secured credit cards: Whether a secured or unsecured card is best for your business depends on your credit history. A typical credit card is unsecured, which means your credit limit isn't tied to any collateral; instead, it's determined by your credit report. Secured credit cards tend to have less strict eligibility requirements because you must offer collateral in the form of a security deposit, which often acts as your credit limit. For example, you might put down $1,000 as your deposit and then have a $1,000 credit limit.

Corporate cards: A corporate card is a specific type of business card typically only available to incorporated businesses, such as corporations and some limited liability companies (LLCs). These cards tend to have stricter eligibility requirements based on company size and available assets.

Who qualifies for a business credit card?

Just about anyone with a business, even a new business, can apply for a business credit card. That includes anyone who operates a sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, or LLC.

This doesn't just include traditional business owners. Sole proprietors could include any number of people who earn money independently, such as freelancers and people who work side hustles.

You might not qualify for a business credit card if you don't have an income-earning venture or side gig. But remember that it's probably easier than you think to meet the qualifications to apply for a business card, especially if you have a good personal credit history.

What to look for in a business credit card

The best credit card for business depends on your preferences and personal finance goals. Consider these factors to help find a card that suits your business needs:

Credit requirements: Most business credit cards require a personal guarantee, meaning you need at least a good personal credit score to qualify. Certain cards could require an excellent credit score, so it's worth researching to find a card that aligns with your current financial situation. If your score is lower than you'd like (potentially in the bad credit range), you can use credit cards to boost your credit score.

Fees: Annual fees and foreign transaction fees are common but avoidable, depending on your needs. In general, cards with premium benefits have annual fees, and credit cards with no foreign transaction fees tend to be travel-oriented.

Benefits: Card perks vary by card and issuer. Benefits could include airport lounge access, cell phone protection, travel insurance, and more.

Rewards: Rewards credit cards generally earn points, miles, or cash back. Points and miles are associated with travel redemptions, while cash back can be redeemed for things like statement credits, gift cards, and (sometimes) bank deposits. Many rewards cards offer welcome bonuses, which are great ways to earn loads of points as a new card member.

APR: Ongoing APRs on credit cards are often high, so it's rarely a good idea to carry a balance. However, some business cards provide 0% intro APR offers on purchases, allowing you to avoid high interest rates during the introductory period. This could come in handy if you have a large purchase coming up and want some extra time to pay it off without added interest.

Business credit card applications are similar to personal credit card applications in that you have to provide some personal information. You can also easily fill out an application and apply online. The main difference when applying for a business card is that you must also provide information about your business.

Here's a breakdown of some of the different items you might see on a business card application:

Authorizing officer title: For sole proprietors, you're the owner. If it's a different business setup, you might be a member, partner, president, or another type of officer.

Business structure: Choose between corporation, LLC, nonprofit, partnership, or sole proprietorship. You're likely a sole proprietor if you work for yourself, such as freelancing or doing a side gig.

Legal business name: Your company's name is typically your own if you're a sole proprietor.

Business mailing address: Unless you have a specific business address, this is your home address.

Business phone number: If you don't have a business phone number, you can use your personal number.

Tax ID type: If you're a sole proprietor, you might not have an employer identification number (EIN), so you can use your Social Security number (SSN).

Number of employees: Sole proprietors typically have only one employee (themselves). Consider how many employee cards you want to give out.

Business established date: This is when your business was created. This doesn't necessarily mean the date you started making money, as the start of your business is when you began setting it up.

Annual business revenue: This is your last year of business revenue. If your business is new, you can put "$0" or an amount you're projected to earn.

Business category: Select the categories most aligned with your business from the available options.

Estimated monthly spend: How much you expect to spend on your business credit card each month.

If you have a legitimate business, even if it's a side hustle, consider applying for a business credit card. Business cards can provide useful features for earning rewards on your top business expenses and keeping those costs separate from your personal spending.

Like with any credit card, you should make sure you use your business credit card responsibly. These cards carry very high APRs which can cost your business a lot of money if you carry a balance.

Remember, business credit cards are meant for business owners, so you likely won't qualify if you don't have some sort of business income or a plan to have business income. Many business card issuers check your personal credit history to see if you qualify, which means you can be approved even if your business is brand new.

Frequently asked questions (FAQs) for business credit cards

Still not sure if a business credit card is right for you? Learn more with these FAQs:

Can you use an EIN to get a credit card?

It's possible to apply for and get approved for a business credit card with just an EIN, but it likely won't be feasible for most small business owners. This is because many EIN-only cards are corporate cards with strict eligibility requirements, such as having a high minimum cash balance of $50,000 or more.

What should your personal credit score be to get a business credit card?

You typically need a good to excellent personal credit score (at least a 670 FICO score) to qualify for a business credit card. Many small business owners don't have much or any business credit history, so business card lenders often do a hard credit check on your personal credit history to assess your creditworthiness.

Does applying for a business card hurt credit?

Most credit card issuers do a hard credit inquiry to check your personal credit report when you apply for a new business credit card. Hard inquiries could initially drop your credit score by a few points but typically won't impact your credit score longer than 12 months.

Which is the easiest business credit card to get?

Qualifying for secured business credit cards is often easier because of more relaxed eligibility requirements. However, you generally have to put down a security deposit as your spending limit. Also, many secured credit cards have fewer benefits than their unsecured counterparts.

Does a business credit card offer federal consumer protections?

Small business credit cards don't qualify for the same consumer protections offered by the Credit Card Accountability Responsibility and Disclosure Act of 2009 (CARD Act). That includes limits to certain fees and charges to cardholders.

Is it easy for an LLC to get a credit card?

You can qualify for a business credit card with an LLC, sole proprietorship, corporation, or another eligible business structure. Startups and other new businesses can qualify because your eligibility for most business cards depends on credit factors, such as your personal credit score, income, and debt.

Some credit cards have annual fees, while others don't. In general, cards with annual fees tend to have more benefits, and you would need to use those benefits to help offset the cost of card membership each year. If you want to keep it simple, you can apply for cards with no annual fees.

What to look for in a Capital One credit card

Eligible new cardholders can earn a credit card sign-up bonus and get a huge head start on earning loads of cash back or travel rewards. It makes sense to apply for a card with a welcome bonus if you know you already have upcoming expenses to help you meet the spending requirement.

Capital One offers various rewards credit cards that earn cash back or miles, each with a different rewards rate. Depending on your preferences, you'll need to choose between cash-back or travel rewards and then figure out how you want to earn those rewards.

For example, some Capital One cards provide flat rates where you earn the same amount on all eligible purchases, while others have specific bonus categories, such as restaurants, where you can earn elevated rewards.

Capital One has a decent lineup of 0% APR credit cards, which could come in handy if you have an upcoming large purchase to make and you want to avoid interest charges for a certain period of time.

If you're looking to pay down debt, you can avoid high interest rates by choosing a balance transfer credit card with a 0% intro APR offer on balance transfers.

Capital One has a large selection of no-annual-fee credit cards, allowing you to earn rewards and take advantage of different card benefits without having to pay an annual membership fee.

Capital One also has cards with annual fees that provide more perks and benefits, but you should determine whether they could provide you with enough value to make the fee worth it.

Just about any credit card can help you build your credit history if you use it responsibly, but people who don't already have an established credit file can't immediately qualify for top-rated cash-back or travel credit cards.

For this reason, Capital One offers secured credit cards and student credit cards. These cards are typically easier to qualify for, and they can still provide valuable rewards and, perhaps more importantly, help you build your credit.

Foreign transaction fees are typically 3% added to your purchase amount for using a credit card to make a foreign transaction. For example, you might incur foreign transaction fees if you're using your credit card in another country.

If you're planning to travel abroad, a credit card with no foreign transaction fees is essential to avoiding these additional charges. Many Capital One cards offer this benefit.

Travel rewards: Cards like the Venture Rewards and Venture X focus on earning travel rewards on everyday purchases and providing travel-related perks and benefits, such as a credit for the TSA PreCheck or Global Entry application fee. Capital One travel cards tend to have lower annual fees than many premium travel cards from other issuers.

No annual fee: Multiple Capital One cards, including the VentureOne Rewards, have no annual fee. This means there's no annual membership cost as a cardholder.

Cash back: Cards like the Capital One Savor and Quicksilver focus on earning elevated cash-back rates on everyday purchases. These cards typically have low or no annual fees.

Low intro APR: These cards offer introductory APRs as low as 0% on purchases and/or balance transfers.

Credit-building: These cards typically have less-strict eligibility requirements, making them good options if you're looking to build or rebuild your credit.

Student: These cards are designed for students looking to establish their credit history.

Business: These cards are for small business owners looking to earn rewards on business expenses.

Should I open a Capital One credit card?

Capital One credit cards make sense if you:

Already have a relationship with Capital One

Want to use some of the best cash-back, travel, and 0% APR cards available

Want low annual fees (compared to some direct competitors)

Want to take advantage of Capital One transfer partners

Prefer online banking or already live near in-person branches

Capital One cards provide plenty of options for various financial goals and preferences. Whether you want to earn cash back or travel rewards, or take advantage of a 0% introductory APR offer, there's a suitable card available. From our experience and research, Capital One is easily one of the best credit card issuers in the U.S. market, able to compete with companies like Chase and American Express with its product offerings.

Capital One Financial Corporation was founded in 1988 and had its initial public offering in 1994. Today, the company is known for its various financial services and products, including credit cards, bank accounts, and loans.

As of June 30, 2025, the Federal Reserve listed Capital One as the sixth-largest U.S. commercial bank by consolidated assets.

Which Capital One credit card is the best?

It depends on your personal finance goals and preferences, but these are the best Capital One cards in their respective categories:

Capital One Savor Cash Rewards Credit Card: Best for cash back, 0% APR, and balance transfers

Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card: Best for travel

Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card: Best for hotels

Capital One Venture X Business: Best for business

Capital One Savor Student Cash Rewards Credit Card: Best for students

Do Capital One cash-back rewards expire?

Capital One credit card rewards don't expire as long as your account is open and in good standing. You can lose any unused rewards if you close your account.

How do I book a trip through Capital One Travel?

Follow these steps to book a trip through Capital One Travel:

1. Navigate to the Capital One Travel site at travel.capitalone.com .

2. Log in with your Capital One online account information.

3. Select the type of travel you want to book between "Flights," "Stays," "Packages," "Rental Cars," and "Premium Stays."

4. Enter your preferred travel details, including destination, dates, and number of travelers.

7. Pay for your booking using your Capital One credit card or Capital One rewards.

How do I increase my credit limit with Capital One?

You can request a credit limit increase through your Capital One online account. This won't harm your credit score because Capital One only uses soft inquiries for these requests. You may be asked to provide information, such as your total annual income, employment status, monthly housing costs, and more.

Alternatively, you may qualify for an automatic credit line increase by responsibly using your Capital One credit card and keeping your financial information updated.

To choose a new card from any credit card company — including Chase — look for the options that best fit your financial goals and credit needs.

Start with the type of card, for instance. If you're looking to pay down existing debt, you'll probably want to prioritize a card with a 0% intro APR for balance transfers over a premium Chase travel card with a high annual fee. Or, if you don't travel much but you still want to earn rewards, you might look for a great cash-back card over one that earns Chase Ultimate Rewards points.

Think about your budget, too. A card with plenty of perks and a very high annual fee may not be worth it if you won't get enough value back to justify the cost. On the other hand, if you're a frequent traveler and want help saving money and time when you travel, those perks could be well worth the fee.

You can also look back at your past purchases to find where you spend the most. Review your credit card statements or banking statements from the past several months. Then, you can nail down exactly where your money goes each month to make sure you get a card with rewards categories that give you the biggest return.

And as a new cardholder, you can also benefit from great Chase credit card bonuses. These welcome bonus offers can offer hundreds — if not thousands — of dollars in Chase rewards value that you can put toward a future trip, your statement balance, and more. You must meet a spending threshold within a certain timeframe to score the welcome offer deal. But with some planning, you can budget your upcoming spending so you both score your Chase credit card bonus and avoid carrying a balance.

Finally, don't forget to look for the smaller Chase credit card perks and protections you may get. If you order food and groceries often, for example, look for the Chase cards that offer DoorDash and Instacart benefits, including complimentary membership and discounts. For frequent travelers, no foreign transaction fees could be an important feature. Many Chase credit cards also include a range of travel and purchase protections; it's worth reading exactly what coverage plans your potential new card has in case you need to use them in the future.

What credit score do you need for a Chase credit card?

In many cases, you'll need at least a good credit score and up to an excellent credit score to get approved for a Chase card. That generally includes credit scores from 670 to the max 850.

Chase does have one card designed for new cardholders: the Chase Freedom Rise℠. It's a no-annual-fee cash-back card with some added benefits to help you build and maintain good credit.

Otherwise, many of Chase's credit cards are rewards credit cards or travel credit cards with stricter requirements for approval. If you're not sure you'll get approved, see if you have any preapproval options. While Chase doesn't currently offer preapproval online, you may be targeted for offers in the mail or online, especially if you already have another account with Chase.

What is the Chase Ultimate Rewards program?

Chase rewards credit cards earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points. If you're thinking about applying for a Chase credit card, it's important to understand this flexible rewards program and how you can maximize the points you earn. In general, Chase credit card points are worth 1 cent each, though some cards may offer higher value for certain redemptions, and transfer values can vary.

Here's a look at the Chase rewards credit cards that earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points:

Chase's co-branded cards with airlines, hotels, and retailers do not earn Chase Ultimate Rewards. You'll need to review the specific loyalty program — such as Southwest Rapid Rewards or World of Hyatt — for your redemption options with those cards.

If you have a Chase Sapphire Preferred, Chase Sapphire Reserve, or Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card, you can get a boosted redemption value when you use your Chase Ultimate Rewards points to book travel through Chase Travel. Chase Sapphire Reserve points get a boost up to 2x, while Sapphire Preferred cardholders get up to a 1.75x boost. Ink Business Preferred cardmembers can also earn more when they redeem for travel through Chase Travel.

Using points to book airfare, hotels, rental cars, and more through Chase Travel is one of the best ways to get maximum value for your Chase points no matter which card you choose. But you'll also have the option to redeem points for cash back, gift cards, toward select eligible purchases, and more.

Not every Chase rewards credit card has the option to transfer points to airline and hotel partner programs. Just like with the boosted Chase Travel redemptions, only the Chase Sapphire Preferred, Chase Sapphire Reserve, and Ink Business Preferred cards offer partner transfers.

Points typically transfer at a 1:1 ratio, but the exact value can vary depending on the travel partner program's redemption value. Here are Chase's current airline and hotel transfer partners:

While credit cards from Chase can offer major savings and benefits for your spending, they're not the only type of account you can open with the bank.

Chase is the largest commercial bank in the U.S. according to Federal Reserve data , with more than $3.5 trillion in assets. In addition to Chase credit cards, you can open various bank accounts (checking, savings, CDs), take on a mortgage loan or auto loan, and even invest through J.P. Morgan.

Use Chase's online locator tool to find information about the more than 4,700 branch locations and 15,000 ATMs — including Chase Bank opening hours, how to schedule a meeting with a representative, and where to find Chase-compatible ATMs abroad.

Chase credit card frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Use these frequently asked questions about Chase credit cards to help choose the right one for you:

There's no universal best credit card from Chase that works for every type of cardholder. Some Chase credit cards may better suit your wallet than others.

If you have existing debt that you want to pay down over an introductory 0% APR period, for example, you might go with the Chase Slate Edge Card. If you're more focused on maximizing travel spending, the Chase Sapphire Preferred Card could be a better option. Or maybe you don't travel much and instead want to make the most of your daily purchases; a Chase Freedom Unlimited or Chase Freedom Flex, then, may be your top pick.

Chase credit cards are consistently among our lists of best credit cards. Whether you're looking for cash-back rewards, travel benefits, a 0% APR, small business savings, or some other credit card offering — there's likely a Chase card for you.

While Chase credit cards are good for many cardholders, you should still make sure you compare credit cards from different card issuers to find the one that works best for your financial goals and budget.

The Chase Sapphire Reserve is one of the most premium rewards credit cards you can get from Chase. It has solid rewards on travel, annual credits, benefits for frequent travelers, and more.

Make sure to review all you'll get from the card — rewards, travel credits, partner benefits, airport lounge access, and more — and compare it with your own spending and travel preferences before you apply.

A credit card sign-up bonus is a reward you can earn as a new cardholder on a rewards credit card. You usually must meet a spending requirement to earn a welcome bonus, often rewarded as cash back, points, or miles. For example, earn 60,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 in the first three months after account opening.

How do credit card sign-up bonuses work?

The requirements can vary by the welcome offer, credit card issuer, and credit card, but you typically have to spend a certain amount of money on your card within a specific period to earn a bonus.

It's common for welcome offer spending requirements to give you a three-month period to earn the bonus, but some periods can last for six months or more. The amount of money you must spend for the bonus can vary, but often ranges from $500 to $4,000.

Many business credit card card welcome offers have higher spending requirements, sometimes reaching $15,000 or more in the same amount of time.

You won't earn the welcome bonus if you don't meet the spending requirements within the given timeframe. One thing to be aware of is that having any of your expenses credited back because of canceled or returned purchases could affect whether you qualify for a bonus.

Who qualifies for a credit card sign-up bonus?

Credit card sign-up bonus requirements can include:

Approval: You must apply and be approved for a card to qualify for its welcome offer. This could include having a sufficient credit score to be eligible for approval.

Previous bonus requirements: You might not qualify for a bonus offer if you've earned a similar offer recently, such as within the last 24 or 48 months.

Similar card requirements: You might not qualify for a bonus offer if you have or have had the same or a similar credit card.

Spending requirements: To earn a welcome bonus, you must spend a certain amount on your card within a specific timeframe.

What to look for in a credit card sign-up bonus

Consider these factors when reviewing credit card sign-up bonuses:

Type of reward: Cash back, points, and miles are the most common reward types. If you're interested in travel, consider points or miles. Otherwise, cash back is the recommended option.

Rewards value: Not all rewards currencies are the same, so it's worth researching the estimated value of a currency when researching different welcome offers. For example, 100,000 points on one card could equal $1,000, but the same number of points on another card might be worth $1,500 toward travel on another card.

Your monthly budget: Going beyond your usual spending habits to earn a welcome offer doesn't make sense in most situations. For this reason, you should calculate your everyday expenses, such as buying groceries and filling up at gas stations, to see if your typical budget can help you meet the spending requirements for a bonus.

Should I open a new credit card for its sign-up bonus?

It's worth looking into the best sign-up bonuses if you have large upcoming purchases. This strategy lets you earn valuable rewards without overspending. However, it's also worth considering a card's other perks and benefits to see if they can bring you long-term value.

Are credit card welcome bonus offers taxable?

You typically aren't taxed for earning a credit card welcome bonus. You might incur taxes if you earned a bonus without spending money or earned rewards in other ways, such as referral bonuses, without spending anything.

articles.body:
As we approach the end of 2026, the S&P 500 index is hovering near an all-time high. However, there are still some attractive opportunities on the table, even in the red-hot artificial intelligence (AI) space.

SentinelOne (NYSE: S) is a leading cybersecurity company that relies heavily on AI to deliver highly automated protection to its enterprise customers. Its stock has soared by 47% so far this year, but it's still much cheaper than its top competitors CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks .

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Investors can scoop up a single share in SentinelOne for under $25. Here's why it could be a great addition to a diversified portfolio before this year is over.

AI can be a powerful tool for enterprises, but it also broadens the attack surface for hackers. Every time a business deploys an AI chatbot or agent, it compromises the safety of its sensitive data and valuable digital assets, which is why businesses need state-of-the-art protection.

SentinelOne's Singularity platform is a holistic solution designed to secure endpoints (computers and devices), cloud networks, employee identities, AI applications, and more. It not only protects against breaches but also offers powerful remediation features to help enterprises restore their networks after a successful attack, minimizing downtime.

On the AI security front, SentinelOne has developed critical new tools, such as Prompt Security. It's designed to protect against new-age attacks like prompt injection, where hackers try to manipulate chatbots and agents into handing over sensitive data by disguising malicious commands as legitimate prompts. Prompt Security also inventories every chatbot and agent deployed by the enterprise, so it immediately knows if an unauthorized application is trying to orchestrate a breach.

Then there is Purple AI, an agentic assistant embedded into the Singularity platform. SentinelOne knows human analysis is no match for modern attack speed, so it designed Purple AI with advanced reasoning to autonomously investigate and take action when threats arise.

SentinelOne had $1.2 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) at the conclusion of its recent fiscal 2027 second quarter (ended July 31), an increase of 22% compared to the year-ago period. However, the company said the ARR attributable to AI products such as Purple AI and Prompt Security nearly tripled , so it's clear that enterprises are prioritizing this new-age protection.

What to look for in a credit card to pay for streaming purchases

Many cards offer credits for purchasing specific streaming subscriptions, making it one of the easiest ways to reduce your streaming expenses. In some cases, you can completely cover the cost of a streaming plan.

It's also important to realize that certain card benefits could indirectly offer a streaming perk. For example, the Amex Platinum provides a monthly credit to cover eligible Walmart+ memberships. If you look at the benefits that come with Walmart+, you'll see you can get a free Paramount+ or Peacock subscription as a Walmart+ member.

Earning increased rewards on streaming purchases is a straightforward way to reduce the cost of your streaming subscriptions. Many cards offer 1.5x or 2x back on streaming purchases, but the better rewards rates are at least 3x back or higher.

Keep in mind that you can also get plenty of value from non-streaming-related spending categories attached to a rewards card. For example, a card might offer increased cash back or points on groceries, in addition to streaming services, providing you with multiple ways to enhance your card's value.

If your goal is to save money on your streaming subscriptions, an annual fee is essentially doing the opposite. You would have to calculate whether taking advantage of certain card benefits would provide enough value to warrant paying a yearly fee.

A credit card sign-up bonus or welcome offer is an excellent way for new cardholders to earn a substantial statement credit or a portion of rewards in a relatively short period. Welcome bonuses can vary greatly depending on the card and card issuer, so it's worth comparing various cards to see what's being offered at any given time.

Should I open a credit card to pay for streaming services?

Opening a credit card to pay for streaming services may make sense if it also helps you accomplish other goals. None of the cards we've included on our list are designed explicitly for making streaming purchases. Instead, they're designed to serve multiple purposes, such as helping you earn rewards on both streaming and grocery purchases.

For example, the Amex Blue Cash Everyday can help reduce the cost of a Disney+ subscription or bundle. In addition, you can also use it to earn increased cash back at U.S. supermarkets and U.S. gas stations. It also comes with a 0% introductory APR offer and has no annual fee.

So, the streaming benefit is one aspect of the card that should be considered, but it also makes sense to think about the card's other perks and how they might help you reach your goals.
